explanation: Ferdinand von Richthofen coined the German Seidenstrasse. Silk was only one cargo: paper, glass, horses and religions such as Buddhism travelled the same routes.

claims.text: The German geographer Ferdinand von Richthofen coined the term Seidenstrasse, Silk Road, in 1877.
The Amber Road, the Incense Route and the Spice Route are names for other trade routes, not the name Richthofen coined in 1877.
Goods such as paper, glass and horses, and religions such as Buddhism, spread along the Silk Road routes.
